questions.question: How do you stay productive when working from home?
questions.intention: Self-management: do you have a real system or just good intentions?
questions.intentionPersian: خودمدیریتی: سیستم واقعی داری یا فقط نیت خوب؟
questions.structure: Concrete habits: workspace, schedule, focus technique, boundaries. One sentence each.
questions.example: I have a dedicated workspace and a fixed routine — I start at the same time every day. I time-block deep work in the morning and keep meetings in the afternoon, and my family knows my door-closed rule.
followUps: What's your biggest distraction and how do you handle it?

questions.question: How do you manage your time across tasks without supervision?
questions.questionPersian: بدون نظارت، زمان‌تان را چطور مدیریت می‌کنید؟
questions.intention: Can they trust you with autonomy?
questions.intentionPersian: آیا می‌شود با استقلال کامل به تو اعتماد کرد؟
questions.structure: Your planning cadence + how your progress stays visible to others without being asked.
questions.example: Every Monday I plan the week against team priorities, and I keep my task board updated daily — my manager never has to ask what I'm doing. If something will slip, I flag it the moment I know.
followUps: What tools do you use for this?

questions.question: How do you handle asynchronous communication with your team?
questions.questionPersian: ارتباط غیرهم‌زمان با تیم را چطور مدیریت می‌کنید؟
questions.intention: Async maturity: writing clearly, not blocking on replies.
questions.intentionPersian: بلوغ در کار غیرهم‌زمان: نوشتن شفاف و منتظرنماندن برای پاسخ.
questions.structure: Write with full context, propose a default ('I'll do X unless you object by...'), keep moving.
questions.example: I write messages with full context so no follow-up round is needed, and I include a default: 'I'll go with option A unless someone objects by tomorrow.' That way time zones never block me.
followUps: When do you decide something needs a call instead?

questions.question: Have you worked across time zones? How did you make it work?
questions.questionPersian: با اختلاف ساعت کار کرده‌اید؟ چطور مدیریتش کردید؟
questions.intention: Practical experience with overlap windows and handoffs.
questions.intentionPersian: تجربه عملی با پنجره‌های هم‌پوشانی و تحویل کار.
questions.structure: Name the real gap you worked across + your overlap/handoff routine.
questions.example: My last team had a four-hour gap with Europe. We kept two core overlap hours for syncs, and I ended each day with a short written handoff — what's done, what's blocked, what I need — so their morning started without waiting for me.
followUps: What was the hardest part of that setup?

questions.question: How do you report progress when nobody sees you working?
questions.questionPersian: وقتی کسی کارتان را نمی‌بیند، پیشرفت را چطور گزارش می‌دهید؟
questions.intentionPersian: شفافیت فعالانه بدون نیاز به مدیریت ذره‌بینی.
questions.structure: A fixed rhythm (daily written update / weekly demo) + the rule 'bad news travels fastest'.
questions.example: I post a short daily update — done, next, blockers — and demo working software every Friday. And my personal rule: bad news travels fastest; if something's off track, my manager hears it from me first.
followUps: How much detail do you include?

questions.question: How do you keep remote meetings effective?
questions.questionPersian: جلسات آنلاین را چطور موثر نگه می‌دارید؟
questions.intentionPersian: نظم جلسات — دستور جلسه، مشارکت، خروجی.
questions.structure: Before (agenda), during (on-topic, camera, notes), after (action items in writing).
questions.example: No agenda, no meeting — that's my rule even when I'm the junior person asking. During the call I take notes, and afterwards I post the action items with owners. Half our meetings became messages, which everyone loved.
followUps: How do you handle people who dominate calls?

questions.question: What do you do when you're blocked and your teammates are offline?
questions.questionPersian: وقتی کارتان گیر کرده و هم‌تیمی‌ها آفلاین‌اند چه می‌کنید؟
questions.intentionPersian: خلاقیت در رفع مشکل در برابر بیکار نشستن.
questions.structure: Timebox your own attempts → document the question with context → switch to a parallel task.
questions.example: I give myself a timebox to find a workaround. If I'm still stuck, I write the question down with everything I tried, post it, and switch to a parallel task — so their answer lands on a well-formed question, and my day isn't lost.
followUps: Give me a real example of that happening.

questions.question: How do you build relationships with colleagues you've never met in person?
questions.questionPersian: با همکارانی که حضوری ندیده‌اید چطور رابطه می‌سازید؟
questions.intention: Remote teams die without intentional connection — do you invest in it?
questions.intentionPersian: تیم دورکار بدون ارتباط عمدی می‌میرد — آیا برایش وقت می‌گذاری؟
questions.structure: Deliberate habits: 1:1 virtual coffees, non-work channels, being generous with help.
questions.example: I book a short virtual coffee with every new teammate, keep my camera on in meetings, and I'm active in the non-work channels. Helping someone debug at 6pm their time builds more trust than any team event.
followUps: How do you notice when a remote colleague is struggling?

questions.question: How do you separate work and personal life when both happen at home?
questions.questionPersian: وقتی کار و زندگی هر دو در خانه است، چطور جدایشان می‌کنید؟
questions.intention: Burnout prevention — sustainable remote workers have boundaries.
questions.intentionPersian: پیشگیری از فرسودگی — دورکار پایدار مرز مشخص دارد.
questions.structure: Honest boundaries: fixed end ritual, notifications policy, the exception rule for real emergencies.
questions.example: I have a shutdown routine — I write tomorrow's top three tasks, close the laptop, and leave the room. Work notifications are off after seven except for production alerts. Remote work made me overwork at first; these rules fixed it.
followUps: What happens when a deadline collides with those boundaries?

questions.question: Why do you want a remote position?
questions.intention: Checking your reasons are about work quality, not avoiding work.
questions.intentionPersian: بررسی اینکه دلیلت کیفیت کار است، نه فرار از کار.
questions.structure: Positive reasons (focus, global teams, proven remote track record) — never 'I don't like offices'.
questions.example: Three reasons: my deep-work output is measurably better without an open office, I want to work with international teams — which is also why I invest in my English — and I've already proven I deliver remotely in my current role.
followUps: What's the biggest downside of remote work for you?
